title: Formations: fewer and thicker, or the same comb?
question: Ignoring the grey light-blocks — do the stalactites and stalagmites in one of these read as rock with a taper, rather than scratches? And is either one still 'totally full of stuff'?
context_md:
Same cave, same seed, same camera and crop, flat lighting so shape is
readable. **Ignore the big grey rectangles** — that is the light-block bug
you flagged ("very large uniform gray blocks with blurry light"), it is
unfixed in both shots, and it is what I am on next. This card is only
about the stone.

Your words on the first one: *"they are all 1 pixel thick. They should
have a taper and be thicker but fewer of them"*, and the cave is
*"totally full of stuff"*.

Measured over 16 seeds, wetland, with an instrument I had to rewrite
first — the old one defined a formation as a column with empty space on
both sides, which is a fine definition while everything is one pixel wide
and exactly wrong once things taper. It was reporting the new formations
as *shorter* while they were getting bigger, and an earlier version of the
work had already been shaped around that bad number.

|                    | one | other |
|---|---|---|
| formations/system  | 45.8 | 15.4 |
| base width, median | 1 | 3 |
| base width, p90    | 1 | 6 |
| height p90         | 19 | 18 |
| height max         | 45 | 45 |
| floor-to-ceiling columns | 181 | 99 |

"Base width median 1, p90 1" is your "all 1 pixel thick", in a number.

The cave passages themselves are untouched between the two shots.
